Q: Enforcing a 2 second delay on Web API call? A:

This is a classic X,Y problem, why do you need exactly 2000ms response from a web api?

Your observation is consistent with expectation, 2007 is really close to 2 seconds, to get closer you would have to take into account how long the additional processing of the response takes (we can't see what other middle ware you have registered), how long serialization of the payload takes and how long the transmission to the client as well as transmission time, deserialization and other processing on the client before the test is evaluated.

We can't tell here but you will also need to make sure your delay middleware executes after your controller action has completed.

You should also consider asynchronous programming as the async/await pattern at runtime allows for task managed to pause your task if it needs to execute other tasks at the same time.

Further to this, using a server-side middleware to add a delay so you can test server-side caching is not a good strategy... It's quite silly actually. Your test should perform the delays at the client.

Q: Pins seem to be involved in the conflict. Currently pinned specs: - python 3.12.* (labeled as 'pin-1') A:

You need to download the preceding version of the python version tagged with the pin in conflict. In your case it is 3.12, so you need python 3.11.

conda install python=3.11 jupyter

Q: How can I search and play a video on YouTube using Selenium in Python? A:

You could bypass the need of starting off at the homepage completely by appending the desired search query to the search_query parameter :)

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.common.keys import Keys
from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
driver.maximize_window()

wait = WebDriverWait(driver, 3)
presence = EC.presence_of_element_located
visible = EC.visibility_of_element_located

# Navigate to the URL with the video being appended to search_query
driver.get('https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query={}'.format(str(video)))

# Play the video
wait.until(visible((By.ID, "video-title")))
driver.find_element(By.ID, "video-title").click()

Q: optimizing function over two variables generates zero-valued hessian? A:

From a code standpoint ("why is the hessian matrix just zeros for my function?"), your function indexes on 0, which R doesnt support, and so x[0] will return numeric(0). Change your function to:

NeglogLikNorm <- function(x) {
  m <- x[1]
  sd <- x[2]
  -sum(dnorm(X, m, sd, log = TRUE))
}

And running the rest of your code will return:

# > MLE.optim.par
# [1] 0.1348410 0.9779023
# > MLE.optim.var
#               [,1]          [,2]
# [1,]  9.562929e-03 -3.352886e-10
# [2,] -3.352886e-10  4.781432e-03

From a math standpoint ("why is the hessian matrix just zeros for my function?"), numeric(0) causes the likelihood to always return 0 so all second-derivative estimates are zero and the Hessian is returned as a matrix of zeros.

Q: How can I get a specific section inside a man page? A:

At the end of a man page, you may find something like a command(some-number) where that (some-number) is the section that contains that command in man pages, so I use the -K switch (note it is a big K), followed by the specified section number, and it works for me:

man -K section_number  term_or_command

I.e.,

man -K 5 /etc/host.conf
